title: Icon Headings with Descriptions (Option 2: icons listed on Special Symbols page)

illustrates.quote: Icons may be assigned a transcriber-defined shape and listed on the Special Symbols page.

blocks.text: Full Text of Icon Descriptions in Front of Book
blocks.features: Plain bold caption labelling the icon-key strip beneath it; excluded from the model (see Option 1).

blocks.text: Eye Safety: Proper eye protection must be worn at all times by anyone performing or observing science activities.
Clothing Protection: This symbol appears when substances could stain or burn clothing.
Animal Safety: This symbol appears when safety of animals and students must be ensured.
Radioactivity: This symbol appears when radioactive materials are used.
Handwashing: After the lab, wash hands with soap and water before removing goggles.

blocks.features: Plain bold caption; excluded from the model.

Bold heading on a shaded banner, followed immediately in print by three small icon graphics (Eye Safety, Clothing Protection, Handwashing). THIS option represents the three icons with transcriber-defined shape codes, listed on the volume's Special Symbols page, per rule 4.9.2.b -- a braille-only convention with no literal print-text equivalent (see uncertain).

Three transcriber-defined shape codes for the icons, printed directly after 'Procedure' on the SAME braille line (matching where the icon graphics sit in print), per 4.9.2.b; NOT built into the model (see uncertain) since these ASCII tokens are already-encoded braille, not translatable print text.

blocks.text: 1. Read and complete the lab safety form.
blocks.features: Numbered procedure step beneath the Procedure banner.

print.notes: Option 2 of 2 (subtitled in the source 'Icons are Listed on Special Symbols Page'): the same three icons are represented by transcriber-defined shape-indicator codes ('@$es', '@$cp', '@$hw') immediately after the 'Procedure' heading on a single line, per rule 4.9.2.b -- devised symbols listed on the volume's Special Symbols page rather than spelled out as words.
print.printFeatures: Same print source as Option 1: a colored strip of five icon+caption+description entries, then a "Procedure" heading followed by three small icon graphics and a numbered instruction step.

braille.notes: Line 1 the cell-5 heading 'Procedure' followed, on the SAME line, by three transcriber-defined shape codes ('@$es','@$cp','@$hw' -- Eye Safety/Clothing Protection/Handwashing, matching Option 1's order), each preceded/followed by a blank space per 4.9.1; line 2 the single numbered procedure step.

uncertain: The three shape codes '@$es'/'@$cp'/'@$hw' are read as Eye Safety/Clothing Protection/Handwashing by matching their order to Option 1's spelled-out heading and by the letters themselves; not cross-checked against an actual Special Symbols page (none is included in this excerpt) or a UEB transcriber-defined-shape reference.

The shape codes are literal, already-encoded BRF ASCII (a braille-only transcriber convention), not print text -- this print.blocks model has no way to feed pre-encoded braille through Emboss's translate() pipeline (which expects plain text to translate FROM), so this content is recorded as `other` and excluded from the model. Expect gold-run.mjs to report a documented mismatch on line 1 (missing the three shape codes after 'Procedure'), not a bug.
resolution: `illustrates.rule`/`quote` resolved to "4.9.2.b" (both runs already agreed on the rule number in substance, differing only in dot-placement; "4.9.2.b" chosen to match the §11 precedent's dotted-letter-suffix convention) with the specific clause text about Special Symbols page shape codes. `print.blocks` rebuilt from the PDF image the same way as Option 1, with the shape-code content recorded as `other` (documented, not modeled) since it is pre-encoded braille ASCII with no print-text equivalent -- an explicit, evidence-based limitation rather than a guess.
